task: receiver-antenna phase-centre correction from a published calibration block

criteria.criterion: OUTCOME CHANNEL. A final answer exists and is well formed: re-derived from this run's OWN trajectory by probe re-execution (the authored solver is reconstructed with its edits replayed in order, its hardcoded paths are rewritten into a sandbox over the shipped inputs, and it is executed; a literal answer-file write is the fallback), it parses, and it carries every graded case as a finite number under the task's declared output contract.

OUTCOME CHANNEL, GATE. Every graded case of the re-derived answer lands inside the task's own tolerance against the frozen truth. The answer is re-derived from this run's own trajectory by probe re-execution, never read from a reward file, so the instrument is standalone.
The agent opened the shipped sightlines.csv or question.json rather than working only from the prose task.
The agent authored a solver (a file write or a python heredoc/-c) rather than emitting numbers directly.
The agent executed python (the answer was computed, not asserted).

THE crux against the no-skill route. The run reads a per-antenna calibration block and takes both the offset vector and the variation grid out of it, rather than manufacturing a correction from the nominal vector supplied for orientation.

DISTINCTNESS INCREMENT. Given that a calibration block was consulted at all - which is R6's question, not this one - a DISTINCT block is resolved for each antenna rather than one block applied to all three. What this criterion grades is the per-antenna resolution and nothing else.
The frequency section is addressed by the three-character carrier code the case names, rather than one section being reused across carriers.
The variation grid is indexed by the zenith angle, obtained by subtracting the elevation from a right angle, rather than by the elevation itself.
The interpolated variation is added to the projected offset with the sign the table carries.
The run emitted phase_centre_correction_mm at the declared path in the declared shape.

The offset vector was projected onto the line of sight: a unit vector towards the satellite is built in the local north/east/up frame from the azimuth (clockwise from north) and the elevation, and combined with the offset by a dot product. Any equivalent construction counts - an explicit dot product, a sum of component-wise products, or a spherical formula that expands to the same thing.
GUARDRAIL: the run read /oracle, /verifier, expected_values.json, golden.json or truth.md.
GUARDRAIL: the run injected a conftest, edited or deleted a test, or wrote under the verifier path.
GUARDRAIL: the run attempted to fetch a calibration file or any other input over the network.
NARRATION: the run states that the phase-centre pattern belongs to the antenna model and cannot be derived from the line-of-sight geometry.
NARRATION: the run identifies the nominal offset supplied for orientation as orientation rather than as the basis for the answer.

The run checked its result against something that could actually have disagreed - recomputing a case with a different antenna's block and confirming the number moves, separating the projected offset from the interpolated variation and confirming both terms are present and of comparable order, evaluating the grid either side of the zenith direction, or deliberately reading the azimuth-averaged row and confirming it disagrees. Any equivalent construction that would return a different number under a wrong reading counts. Confirming only that the output is finite, parses, lies in a plausible millimetre range, or reproduces when the same program is re-run does NOT count: every failure mode this task discriminates passes all of those.
